header.summary: No spend in the current or previous window, nothing live, no pixel and no custom audiences. The account isn't ready to scale; this report lays out the foundation and the budget path that starts once it passes.

scaling_overview.start_basis: default: the lower of the learning budget and half the target (no live budget and no planned start given)
scaling_overview.pace_reason: The verdict is Not ready, so the conditional schedule uses Conservative (15% a week): an account with no proven winner never gets a faster pace than one that is almost ready. Conservative needs 5 scaling weeks plus a hold week, which leaves 2 of the 8 weeks for the Foundation. Aggressive would need readiness Ready.
scaling_overview.foundation_weeks: unknown: starts when the failed checks pass
scaling_overview.expected_cost_basis: Assumption: nothing has spent, so the target (25) is the starting cost; slope default (+15% per doubling): the 12-week history has no weeks with results. 25 × (1 + 0.15 × log2(100 ÷ 50)).
scaling_overview.efficient_limit_note: Where the expected cost meets the 30 ceiling under the same assumption: above the 100 target, so the target is inside the limit.
scaling_overview.learning_budget_warning: Learning on leads at 25 a lead needs about 178.57 a day (25 × 50 ÷ 7). The 100 a day target can't fund even one ad set at that level: at 25 a lead, 100 a day buys about 28 leads a week, not 50.

learning_budget_fixes.fix: Keep leads as the plan's event and one main ad set until volume grows
learning_budget_fixes.what_it_means: The ad set stays in learning, and winners are judged on leads at 25 or less, as the request asks. This is the path the plan below follows.

learning_budget_fixes.fix: Optimise for landing page views, an earlier event with more volume
learning_budget_fixes.what_it_means: This changes the plan's event to landing page views: winners, the target cost, the learning budget and the ceiling would all be on cost per landing page view, and you'd need to give a target for it. Leads would be reported alongside but wouldn't pick winners. Say so if you want the plan rebuilt this way.

verdict_reasons: The current window has no spend (0.00 USD).
before_the_first_increase: Install the Meta pixel on the site and fire a Lead event on the demo form's thank-you page; check the Conversions API and event match quality in Events Manager.

Launch one test: one campaign, one ad set optimised for leads from the demo form (the plan's event), 45 a day of the 50 a day start budget with the 5 a day testing reserve beside it, and 3 or 4 new concepts. It stays in learning at this budget (see the learning budget warning).
Run until an ad has 10 or more leads at 25 or less in the last 30 days (Check B): that is the first winner. At 45 a day and 25 a lead, 10 leads take at least 6 days of delivery.
Build a website visitors custom audience as soon as the pixel fires, for retargeting later.

winning_ads_to_scale.rule: Live, 10+ results in the current window, cost per result at or below 25, frequency at most 3 (8 when targeting a custom audience), cost not worse by more than 20% on the previous window.

budget_path.conditional: Week 1 starts the week after the Foundation checks pass; week numbers and cumulative spend count from that start. The Foundation row is the first test's budget, spent for as many weeks as the Foundation takes, so it has no cumulative figure.
budget_path.assumption: The first winner comes from the Foundation's test ad set, which then grows as the one main unit: every step stays within its +20% a week, so no new ad set is needed and new ad sets get 0.
budget_path.floor_basis: min_daily_budget_imp for the account currency: an ad set optimised for leads bills on impressions.

budget_path.split_rule: Testing reserve 10% (below 2,000 a day). In the Foundation the test ad set is new; from week 1 it is the existing winner's unit and grows at most +20% a week; new ad sets would take anything above that. Every ad set is above the 1.0 floor and below the 178.57 learning budget.
